content.title: About
content.content: Durum wheat is a high‑protein variety of wheat used to make puffed grains. The puffed product is created by applying heat and pressure to whole durum kernels, resulting in light, crunchy, airy pieces. They are commonly used in breakfast cereals, snacks, and various recipes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Durum wheat is primarily grown in dry regions such as the Mediterranean and the western United States.
Puffed durum wheat is often incorporated into gluten‑free blends after the gluten is removed.
The heat‑treatment preserves most B‑vitamins and minerals.
Puffed grains serve as a base for energy bars and granola mixes.
Durum wheat is the main raw material for pasta production.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Durum wheat provides about 12‑14 % protein, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Contains complex carbohydrates
items.content: The puffed grains release glucose slowly, helping to sustain energy and fullness.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Provides iron and magnesium
items.content: These minerals are essential for hemoglobin formation and nerve function.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Puffed durum wheat contains virtually no fat, making it suitable for low‑calorie diets.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: People with wheat allergy or celiac disease may experience adverse reactions.

items.title: Contains gluten
items.content: Durum wheat is a gluten source; the product is not appropriate for gluten‑free diets.

items.title: Nutrient loss over time
items.content: Extended storage in poor conditions can reduce vitamin levels.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Puffed grains can be eaten dry as a light snack, added to milk, yogurt or kefir, used in granola, energy bars, and baked goods. Lightly toasting them with honey or spices enhances flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the puffed wheat in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For long‑term storage, refrigerate to maintain crispness and prevent mold growth.
